about.title: What is HeartEats
about.intro: HeartEats is a map of places to eat in Madrid where people with disabilities work. It is meant to help you choose calmly where to go, knowing who is behind it.

sections.heading: Why it exists
paragraphs: Going out to eat is something we all do every day. We like the idea that choosing a place where people with disabilities work can be as simple as any other choice, made for what really matters: tasty food, kind service and a good job.

sections.heading: What you will find here
items: Places with real inclusive employment: what counts is who works there.
Independent businesses and projects with social impact, which are the ones that need visibility most and the ones we can get to know closely.
If you are looking for information about ramps or accessible toilets, there are other tools for that. HeartEats is not a job board either.

sections.heading: How it works
items: Anyone can suggest a place or a correction.
A person reviews each suggestion calmly before it is published.
The business always has the final word: nobody appears on the map without knowing.
Each listing tells you how and when its details were checked.

sections.heading: The people on the team
paragraphs: Each listing talks about the team as a whole. A person’s name, photo or story only appears if they decide so themselves and give their permission, and they can change their mind whenever they like.

sections.heading: Open and non-profit
paragraphs: HeartEats is a non-profit project. Its code is open (AGPL-3.0 licence) and so is the business database (ODbL licence). People’s stories, names and photos are outside that licence. The map relies on open data and always shows where it comes from.

sections.heading: Where we are
paragraphs: We are starting in Madrid and hope to reach more cities little by little. HeartEats is still being built: for now you will see sample places, which do not exist and are marked [DEMO].

verification.title: How we verify
verification.intro: We want every point on the map to be trustworthy. That is why nothing is published until a person has reviewed it and the business itself agrees.

sections.heading: What happens when someone suggests a place
items: We receive the suggestion. It is not public yet.
An automatic filter helps us avoid unwanted messages and spot places that are already on the map.

A person calmly checks that the place exists, that it is independent and that its team is inclusive. They use a link, news coverage, the business’s website, agreements or references from organisations in the sector.

We get in touch with the business through an official channel. We would like to know whether it is happy to appear, and to offer it the chance to tell its team’s story at the level of detail it prefers.
With all this, a decision is made: we publish it, ask for a little more information or, if it does not fit, explain why. Everything is recorded.

sections.heading: What each level means
paragraphs: Places that have not been checked yet do not appear on the map.
items: Verified details: our team has checked them with a visit, a call or documents.
Details confirmed by the community: confirmed by the business itself with some proof, or by several people who do not know each other.

sections.heading: How we check
paragraphs: We use these methods, from strongest to weakest:
items: A visit to the place.
Direct confirmation from the business, by phone or by email from its official domain.
Documents: agreements, certifications or official statements.
References from organisations in the sector.

sections.heading: Which businesses fit
paragraphs: HeartEats focuses on independent businesses and projects with social impact, because they are the ones that need visibility most and the ones we can get to know closely. Large chains and corporate franchises are not part of this map. This is not a judgement of their work or of the people who work there: it is simply the focus we have chosen.
If you are unsure about a case, such as a co-operative, a small group or a social project with several places, tell us: we will look at it calmly, one by one.

sections.heading: Keeping details up to date
items: Each listing shows the level, the method and the date of the last check.
After 12 months, the listing is marked as due for review.
Anyone can suggest a correction or ask for a listing to be removed.
The business can ask for changes or to leave whenever it likes.

sections.heading: We look after your privacy when reviewing
paragraphs: Suggestions from other people do not include details about people on the team. If someone writes them, we leave them out when reviewing. The email of the person making the suggestion is private, and we only use it in case we need to ask them something.

privacy.title: Privacy and data
privacy.intro: This text is a draft: a professional still has to review it and it may change before launch. It is written in plain language, for people who are not lawyers.

sections.heading: In short
items: You can use HeartEats without giving us any data: there are no accounts, we do not use our own cookies and we do not measure your activity.
If you suggest a place or a correction, you tell us what you want about the place. Your email is optional, private, and only used in case we need to ask you something.
We do not publish or keep names or health data of people without their express permission. If someone writes them in a suggestion, we leave them out when we review it.
If a business decides to tell its team story, the business does it, and each person gives their consent. They can withdraw it whenever they want, without giving reasons.

sections.heading: This version is just starting
paragraphs: Suggestions, corrections and removal requests are now really sent and reviewed by a person. The business form for telling a team story is also really sent. The photos of a new place are also really sent; team photos are not asked for yet. What follows describes how we handle data.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for the data
paragraphs: Until an association exists, the person responsible is the person behind the project: Marlon Bermúdez, in a personal capacity. When the association is set up, this section will change. How to write to us is on the Contact page.

sections.heading: What data we handle and why
items: If you use the website: none of our own. The web server and the map server see your IP address when they serve you the page, like any server.
If you tap Near me: your location is used only on your device, to sort places by distance. It is not sent or saved, and it is only requested when you tap the button.

If you suggest a place: the place details, how you know it, a link (optional), photos of the place and of the dishes (optional, with your confirmation that they are yours or you have permission) and your email (optional). We use them to review the suggestion and, if it meets the criteria, publish it. Photos are resized on your device and wait in a private store that only moderators can see; only the ones a person approves one by one are published, and if the suggestion is rejected they are deleted. The suggestion is kept until it is resolved; your email is deleted when it is resolved or after 9 months at the latest.

If you suggest a correction: what needs correcting, your explanation, a link (optional) and your email (optional). We use them to review the notice and, if it is right, update the listing. They are kept like a suggestion.

If you reply to a request for information: the text you write (up to 2000 characters; please do not include health details or other people’s names). It is kept with the proposal to decide on it, and for as long as it. To write to you we use the email you left, and the reply link works only once.

If you request a removal: what you want removed, your explanation (without health data or third-party names) and your email, which is required so we can confirm by email that you are the person or their representative before hiding anything. They are kept like a suggestion; your email is deleted when it is resolved or after 9 months at the latest.
If you are a moderator: your email and the area you moderate, so you can sign in and review suggestions, for as long as you are one.
To prevent unwanted messages: a temporary counter per IP address, kept for a few hours. The hidden field in the form does not store anything about you.

If you are a business and tell your team story: team figures, your email (required, so we can confirm with you that the business is sending it) and, at the highest level, name or pseudonym, role and story of each person, with their permission (photos are not asked for yet). We use them to show the listing with the detail the business chooses. While it is being reviewed, only an administrator reads them; the email is deleted when the request is resolved or after 9 months at most. The stories leave the request once it is resolved: if it is approved, they move to the listing and are kept for as long as the business and the person keep them; if not, they are deleted.
paragraphs: We process your email and what you write in the forms because you give them to us when you send them (your consent). The data of a team member is processed only with that person’s explicit consent.

sections.heading: The people on the team
paragraphs: This section matters most to us, so we explain it in simple words.
items: A suggestion from someone else does not include data about team members. If someone writes names or health data, we leave them out when we review it.
Only the business can tell the story of its team, and never in detail without its knowledge. Until the business confirms, we only show public, verifiable information.
Each person decides for themselves whether to appear, under what name (it can be a pseudonym) and with what photo. Where it applies, their legal representative decides.
A story without recorded consent is not saved.
It can be withdrawn at any time, without giving reasons. The story stops being shown immediately and the data is deleted within 21 days at most.

In small teams (fewer than 5 people) we make sure nobody can be recognised: we do not publish figures by type of disability or by role when they could identify someone, and we only give general figures.
Stories, names and photos are not under an open licence and are never included in open data exports.

sections.heading: Third parties involved
items: Website hosting: Netlify. It records the IP address of whoever visits the site, like any server.
Map: tiles and styles are served by OpenFreeMap. When you open the map, your browser requests them directly and they see your IP address. We send them nothing else.

Email: we use Resend (servers in Ireland, European Union) to send moderation sign-in links and notices to people who left their email (for example, that their suggestion is now published). They see that address and the text of the notice.
Geocoding: to place a business on the map, our server sends its address (street, postal code and city) to Nominatim (OpenStreetMap). It does not send your email or anything about you.

Server and database: the API runs on Railway (Amsterdam, Netherlands) and the database is on MongoDB Atlas (Paris, France), both inside the European Union. They hold the suggestions, contact emails, team stories and the accounts of the people who moderate.
Backups: every week we keep a copy of the database on Cloudflare R2. The copy is encrypted before it leaves and only we hold the key, so Cloudflare cannot read it.
We do not sell or pass on data to anyone.

sections.heading: Open data
paragraphs: The business database is published under the ODbL licence: name, address, type of cuisine, verification level and aggregate figures. It does not include stories, names, photos, emails or data about whoever suggests or corrects.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask us to access your data, correct it, delete it, limit its use, object to it or receive it in a portable format. If you gave us your consent, you can withdraw it at any time, and that does not affect what has already been handled. We will answer within one month at the most. You can also write to us at contact@hearteats.org.
If you ever feel we have not looked after your data well, you can complain to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (aepd.es). Before that, we would love the chance to sort it out with you.

sections.heading: Security
paragraphs: Data is kept on servers with restricted access and an encrypted connection. The email of whoever suggests or corrects is only seen by the moderation team.

sections.heading: Changes to this text
paragraphs: If something important changes, we will update it here and change the date. Version: draft, October 2026.

legal.title: Legal notice
legal.intro: This text is a draft: a professional still has to review it and it may change before launch. It says who is behind HeartEats and the terms for using it.

sections.heading: Who is behind it
paragraphs: HeartEats is an open, non-profit project. Until an association exists, it is run by Marlon Bermúdez, in a personal capacity.
The identification details the law requires (address and tax number) will be added here before launch.

sections.heading: What this site is
paragraphs: A free map of Madrid hospitality businesses that employ people with disabilities. It is for information only: we do not handle bookings, orders or payments.

sections.heading: About the information
items: It is provided by people and businesses, and a person reviews it before it is published. Even so, there may be mistakes or changes we do not know about.
While the website is in testing, the data you see is sample data.
If something is wrong, you can suggest a correction. If something affects you, you can ask for a removal.

sections.heading: Licences
items: The code is free software, under the AGPL-3.0 licence.
The business database is under ODbL, and the documentation under CC BY-SA 4.0.
People’s stories, names and photos have no open licence: they are shown only with their permission and can be withdrawn.
The map uses OpenStreetMap data, © OpenStreetMap contributors.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
paragraphs: Please use it respectfully: do not knowingly send false information, other people’s names or health details without their permission, or flood the forms with automated submissions. We may discard anything that does not follow this.

sections.heading: Responsibility and links
paragraphs: We cannot guarantee that the website will always be available or free of errors. The external pages we link to, such as a place’s own website or the map directions, have their own terms and are not our responsibility.

sections.heading: Applicable law
paragraphs: Spanish law applies.

paragraphs: If something important changes, we will update it here. Version: draft, October 2026.

cookies.title: Cookies and storage
cookies.intro: This text is a draft: a professional still has to review it and it may change before launch. It lists everything HeartEats keeps in your browser.

sections.heading: In short
items: For people who visit the website, HeartEats does not use cookies. Only moderators receive one, needed to keep their session (see below).
There is no analytics, advertising or tracking.
That is why you will not see a cookie notice.
It only stores two things in your browser, and only when you use a feature that needs them: the language you choose and the draft of Suggest a place.

sections.heading: What is kept in your browser
items: Your language: if you change it with the selector in the header, it is remembered for your next visit. It is a two-letter code (es or en) with no expiry date; it is deleted with the site data.

The draft of Suggest a place: while you type, so you do not lose your text if you close the page. It does not include your email, the website or the photos. It is kept for 7 days at most and is deleted when you send it or press Start over.
paragraphs: Everything stays on your device and is not sent to anyone. Your browser keeps it for a feature you asked for, so we do not ask for permission.

sections.heading: The moderation cookie
items: If you are a moderator, when you sign in with the emailed link the server stores a cookie called he_session.
It is only used to keep your session. The website cannot read it (it is httpOnly) and it is not sent to anyone else.
It expires after 7 days without activity or when you press Sign out.
paragraphs: It is essential for you to be able to sign in, so no permission is asked. Nobody else receives it.

sections.heading: What is not kept
items: Your location: it is only used in memory if you press Near me, and is forgotten when you close the page.
Your search and filters: they live in the page address.
The language, as long as you have not chosen one: it is worked out from your browser language on each visit and is not stored.
The photos you choose: they are only held while you fill in the form.

sections.heading: How to delete it
paragraphs: In your browser settings, under site data or local storage. If you delete the draft, you only lose what you had written.

sections.heading: Third parties
paragraphs: When you open the map, your browser asks for it directly from the service that provides it, which sees your IP address. Today it does not set cookies. We also explain this in Privacy and data.

sections.heading: If this changes
paragraphs: If we ever used cookies or analytics, we would say so here first and ask for your permission for anything that is not essential. Version: draft, October 2026.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: There is a route for each need. Almost everything can be done from the website itself.

sections.heading: Suggest a place or correct a detail
paragraphs: Anyone can do it, without an account. A person reviews it calmly before it is published.

sections.heading: If you run a business
paragraphs: Tell us about your team with the level of detail you prefer. You decide how much is told.

sections.heading: Withdraw a story or exercise your rights
paragraphs: To withdraw a story, a photo or a listing, use the form on the website: no account and no explanations needed. We write to the email you leave to confirm it is you.

For any other right over your data, or if you prefer to write to us, use this address. We reply within one month at the most. Please do not include health information or other people’s names in your message.

sections.heading: Website bugs and code
paragraphs: The HeartEats code is open. If you found a bug on the website, you can tell us on GitHub. It is a public site: please do not include personal data.

moderation.adminOnly: An administrator decides this request. You can see it, but not decide it.

moderation.pinHelp: If there is no pin, type the place coordinates (for example, 40.4168 and -3.7038).
moderation.changeHelp: Write only what you have checked. Anything left blank is not touched.
moderation.changeClosed: The place has closed for good (the listing will stop being shown)
moderation.changePinHelp: If the pin is wrong, write the right coordinates (for example, 40.4168 and -3.7038). If you change the address and add them, the pin is not looked up on its own.
moderation.hoursHelp: Write the full schedule: it replaces the current one. Leave a day blank if it is closed.
moderation.storyHelp: Its position on the listing, counting those already withdrawn.

login.intro: Sign in with your moderation email: we send you a link that expires in 15 minutes.
login.sent: If that email belongs to a moderator, the link is already in their inbox. It expires in 15 minutes and can only be used once.
login.limited: Many links have been requested in a short time. Please try again in a little while.
login.error: We could not send the link. Please try again in a moment.
login.invalidLink: The link is not valid or has expired. Request a new one.

staff.title: Who moderates
staff.intro: Invite someone with their email and the place where they can decide. Nothing is sent to them: they sign in by asking for their access link with that same email.
staff.invited: Done: {email} can now ask for their access link.
staff.confirmAsk: Remove access for {email}? They lose access right away; what they did stays in the log.

errors.invalidCountry: The country is two letters, for example ES.
errors.forbidden: You do not have permission to do this.
errors.save: We could not save it. You can try again.
errors.disable: We could not remove access. You can try again.

audit.title: Log
audit.intro: What has been done, most recent first. It keeps no names or stories.
audit.empty: There is nothing in the log yet.
audit.moreError: We could not load more. You can try again.

removal.title: Ask for something to be removed
removal.sendError: We could not send the request. You can try again whenever you like.

whats.story: A story (mine, or one of someone I represent)
whats.data: Something else about my personal data

s1.intro: You can ask without an account and without giving reasons. Anyone who shared their story or photo can withdraw it whenever they want.
s1.question: What would you like us to remove?
s1.error: Choose what you want removed to continue.

s2.intro: Tell us which place it appears on, so we can find it.
s2.place: Which place does it appear on?
s2.details: Anything else that helps us find it?
s2.detailsHint: For example, the name or pseudonym shown. Please do not write health information or other people’s names.

s3.intro: We need an email address to confirm that it is you or your representative. That way nobody can remove anything on someone else’s behalf.
s3.emailHint: Only the moderation team sees it, and it is deleted once the request is handled.
s3.emailError: Enter a valid email address to continue.
s3.consent: By sending it you agree that we use your email only to handle this request. More in

done.title: Request received
done.body: We will write to the email you gave us to confirm it is you. As soon as we have confirmed it, we will remove what you asked for.

load.error: We could not load the data. Please try again in a moment.
load.missingTitle: We could not find this place
load.missingBody: It may no longer be published, or the address may be wrong.

submit.limited: Many requests have been sent from your connection in a short time. No problem: please try again in a little while.

reply.title: Reply to Moderation
reply.intro: Moderation needs one more detail about “{name}” to make a decision.
reply.introNoName: Moderation needs one more detail about your proposal to make a decision.
reply.deadline: You can reply until {date}. If you would rather leave it as it is, you do not need to do anything.
reply.hint: Take your time. Up to 2000 characters.
reply.consent: We keep your reply only to decide on this proposal. More in
reply.invalid: Write your reply before sending it.
reply.limited: Many replies have been sent from your connection in a short time. Please try again in a while.
reply.error: We could not send your reply. Please try again in a moment.

done.title: Thank you for replying!
done.body: We have received your reply and the proposal goes back to the Moderation queue. We will write to you if we need anything else.

invalidLink.title: This link is no longer valid
invalidLink.body: You may have already replied, it may have expired, or Moderation may have sent a newer one. If you want to add something, write to us.
